prompt: Use Humane to write a warm, crisp website introduction in no more than 35 words. It sits under 'Less to read. More to understand.' The MIT license and current private-preview status appear separately. Explain the product and why it matters, not a list of features.

sources.text: Humane is one free, MIT-licensed Agent Skill used with an existing AI assistant. AI makes it easy to produce far more text than people can reasonably read and review. Humane focuses on the person receiving the material: a coherent explanation instead of repeated summaries, useful context, important caveats kept beside claims, and relevant sources to check. It can help prepare drafts or understand received documents. It has no hosted model or account of its own. No measured time savings or guarantee of preserving every fact has been established.

checks: Makes the human reading/review burden central rather than only listing assistant tasks.

prompt: Use Humane to edit this update for library staff. Preserve the operational facts and dependencies, but make it easy to use. Return only the update in no more than 130 words.

sources.text:
## A new chapter in service excellence

It is important to note that a carefully coordinated change is approaching, representing a significant milestone in our ongoing commitment to a seamless library experience. The change will take place on 16 November. This is not merely a technical event; it is a step toward a more connected future.

## Preparing for the transition

Preparation is essential. Staff must sync all loan records before 09:45 and record the synced record count. This preparatory action is vital for ensuring that the loan records have been synced. From 10:00 to 10:20, patrons cannot sign in to the catalogue. During that interval the returns desk stays open, using paper receipts; barcode scans remain stored locally until service returns.

## What happens next

The operations team may switch on the new search only after the permission check passes. If that check fails, keep the old search running and report the failure to the operations lead. Do not switch on the new search first and check permissions later. These steps apply to both branches.

The permission check does not affect the returns desk. No staff overtime has been approved. We have not measured any improvement to service speed yet. The future looks bright as we move forward together. Preparation is the foundation of success.

checks: Organizes the update around useful timing and actions rather than preserving repeated ceremonial sections.
Keeps 16 November, sync before 09:45 with recorded count, and the 10:00–10:20 catalogue sign-in interruption.
Keeps returns open with paper receipts, locally stored barcode scans until service returns, both branches, and no approved overtime.
Keeps the permission check before new-search activation; failure means old search stays running and reporting to the operations lead.
Does not imply returns close or depend on the permission check, and does not invent a measured speed benefit.
Removes repeated setup/closing claims instead of only swapping inflated words for synonyms; uses at most 130 words.
